decisions.decision: Drop the proposed C2 provision requiring full site plan review for minor changes near residential abutters, in favor of relying on the more easily amended site plan regulations.
Keep the inclusionary housing bylaw applicable to ANR lots for now, revisiting if a pattern of small estate-lot subdivisions emerges.
Reinstate a payment-in-lieu option and an offsite-unit option for developers triggering inclusionary housing requirements, with amounts to ramp up with the number of units.
Raise the single-family density cap in the cluster bylaw from two to four units per acre.
Keep the cluster housing minimum parcel size at 10 acres rather than lowering it to 5.
Add explicit language requiring the percolation test be completed before site plan review for cluster developments.
Reframe the cluster buffer as a non-disturbed area rather than a cleared buffer, with the planning board able to require landscaping if the area is already bare/grass.
Allow the required buffer area to count toward the cluster open-space percentage.
Remove letters of credit as an allowed performance guarantee for cluster developments, limiting security to cash, a AAA-rated bond, or a covenant.
Treat cluster developments as a single parcel with an exclusive-use area rather than individual lots, removing the need for a frontage standard.
Do not include an under-18 occupancy exclusion in the senior housing bylaw, so the bylaw remains eligible to carry inclusionary housing requirements.
Require native tree species in the landscaping/shade tree requirements.
Count only conditionable/livable space (not inaccessible attics) toward the senior housing maximum dwelling size cap.
Use a different parking standard than 1.5 spaces per unit for assisted-living-type senior housing, to be developed separately.
Hold the next working session on August 10th from 6:00 to 7:00 PM before the regular hearing agenda.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Planning Board held an off-cycle working session to draft language for four zoning bylaw changes: minor site plan review, inclusionary housing, cluster housing, and a new senior housing bylaw. The board worked through a consultant's draft site plan amendment, discussed how an inclusionary housing bylaw with a payment-in-lieu and affordable housing trust could work alongside a proposed senior housing bylaw, and revised numerous cluster-housing standards (acreage threshold, open space percentage, density, buffers, performance guarantees). No formal votes were taken on the bylaw language itself; the board reached working consensus on several specific provisions and set its next working session for August 10th before adjourning with no public comment offered.

what_happened.line: The board raised the cluster-housing density cap for single-family units from two to four per acre.
It restored a payment-in-lieu option and an offsite-unit option for developers triggering inclusionary housing, ramping with unit count.
A draft requirement for full site plan review on minor changes near residential abutters was dropped in favor of the existing, more easily amended regulations.
Letters of credit were removed as an allowed performance guarantee for cluster developments, leaving cash, a AAA-rated bond, or a covenant.
The board left out an under-18 occupancy restriction from the draft senior housing bylaw so it can still carry inclusionary housing requirements.

why_it_matters: These are working drafts of zoning bylaws headed toward town meeting, and the density, buffer, and guarantee choices made here will set the terms any cluster or senior housing project has to meet.
The inclusionary housing provisions determine whether new development contributes cash or units toward affordable housing, and how much.
